newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wheelock's Hung says EMU raises concerns for Asia.
newsitem.headline: Wheelock's Hung says EMU raises concerns for Asia.

text.p: European leaders must work harder to explain the ramifications of monetary union to Asian business people worried about possible protectionism and other problems, said John Hung, managing director of Wheelock and Co

"Like the U.S., Asia as a whole tends to view this European attempt to establish a monetary union by 1999 with scepticism. This is understandable because education of overseas investors has not been adequately carried out by the European authorities," Hung said at a seminar sponsored by ABN Amro Bank.

Hung cited fears that currency volatility leading up to the 1999 union could hurt global growth, concerns that increased competition in Europe could raise unemployment in the continent and, perhaps most important for Asia, speculation that a fully united Europe could mean increased trade protectionism.
"Fears of European protectionism have already resulted in sizable investments being pre-emptively committed by Japanese and Korean corporations to Europe," said Hung.
Hung also said that "indecisiveness of (some) European economies in respect of joining the EMU in the interim (before 1999) may also produce various opportunities for forex speculators."
"Whether or not the increases in forex volatility produced as a result would impinge negatively on international trade are something that needs to be examined carefully," he said.
Jac Kragt, international economist at ABN Amro Bank NV, said he expects the euro, to come into existence in 1999.
He said the advent of the euro will make Europe's capital markets deeper, broader and more liquid and could present new opportunities for Asian investors and issuers.
